Hi Irene,

Thanks for the follow-up. We're excited to see the demo but ran into a problem — the calendar invite you sent earlier showed up in our Exchange calendar with a blank "Join" field and when we try to accept we get a popup: "You don't have permission to accept this invitation". Michael also tried and hit the same error.

Can we rebook for next Tuesday (Aug 24) late-morning PT? If you have an alternate Zoom link or a direct meeting URL we can use that as a fallback. I've attached a screenshot of the Exchange error.

Samiha

Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Scheduling Redwood demo — calendar invite issue

Hi Samiha — thanks for the detail and the screenshot. Sorry about the friction. We see this occasionally when Exchange/Outlook blocks organizer changes from external ICS files.

Quick plan:
- I will create a Zoom meeting and send a direct join link (public URL) so guests can bypass the problematic ICS.
- I'll also re-export the invite as a fresh invite.ics and attach it here. If Exchange still rejects it, Ben can be added as an alternate host on the Zoom side so we can "claim" the meeting in case the organizer is stripped.

Proposed slot: Tue Aug 24, 10:30–11:00 PT. Does that work for you & Michael?

I've attached: invite.ics (text/ics).
Zoom: https://redwood.zoom.us/j/9876543210

If you prefer a calendar link instead: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=abcdef123456

I'll wait for your go-ahead and will follow up with a short agenda.

Best,
Irene Choi
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood-inference.com

Subject: Re: Scheduling Redwood demo — calendar invite issue

Thanks Irene. We tried the two links you sent: the Google Calendar link shows up correctly for me but when I accept it in Exchange, our system still converts it and shows Redwood as an external organizer with no RSVP control. The Zoom URL opens fine in a browser but our corporate SSO blocks adding alternate hosts unless the organizer is in our allowlist, which is the root of the problem.

Michael suggests two options on our side:
1) We accept the Google event and forward an internal invite from our Exchange organizer (not ideal).
2) You set Ben Carter (ben_carter@redwood-inference.com) as an alternate host on the Zoom meeting so if the organizer gets stripped during the transfer, Ben can claim host/assign co-hosts.

Either will work for us; we prefer option 2 to keep everything clean. Can Ben be added, and can you confirm whether there are any host-claim steps we'll need to do?

Thanks,
Samiha

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood-inference.com>
To: Samiha Noor <samiha@finovasolutions.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Scheduling Redwood demo — calendar invite issue

Hi Samiha — Ben here (Sales). Happy to own the host claim/workaround. I set the Zoom meeting to list me as an "Alternative Host" and confirmed the meeting settings allow alternative hosts to start the meeting and assign co-hosts. If Exchange strips the organizer we can still start the call from our Zoom account and claim host rights.

Steps we took (so your IT can follow if needed):
- Added ben_carter@redwood-inference.com as an alternative host on the Zoom meeting (meeting id: 9876543210).
- Enabled "Allow participants to join before host" is OFF (so we control when the meeting starts).
- Uploaded a fresh invite.ics to the calendar event.

If your Exchange admin needs to make us an allowed external organizer, the easiest debug is to have them accept the event from the Google Calendar link we shared and confirm it doesn't get rewritten. If they prefer, we can also send a calendar invite generated from an @finovasolutions.com organizer address (we'd need a forwarded invite from you to create that).

Attached: alternate-host-guide.pdf (short checklist for Exchange/Zoom host claims).

Confirming the slot: Tue Aug 24, 10:30–11:00 PT — we will stand by and if you accept we'll send a final confirmation + 3-bullet agenda.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood-inference.com
